```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=9, fig.height=5)
set.seed(42)
```

# Data and conversion

The source is the public Replogle et al. K562 essential-gene CRISPRi H5AD (`10.25452/figshare.plus.20029387`). Its legacy AnnData encoding is converted without changing the raw file. From the project root, run `python scripts/prepare_k562_subset.py` to calculate full-dataset QC and write a sparse, modern H5AD. The seeded analysis sample retains at least five cells per perturbation when available, then samples the remaining cells at random to 12,000 cells.

```{r packages}
library(anndataR)
library(Seurat)
library(Matrix)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r import}
path <- "data/processed/01_k562_analysis.h5ad"
stopifnot(file.exists(path))
adata <- read_h5ad(path)
cat("Analysis dimensions (cells x genes):", paste(dim(adata), collapse=" x "), "\n")
cat("obs columns:", paste(colnames(adata$obs), collapse=", "), "\n")
cat("var columns:", paste(colnames(adata$var), collapse=", "), "\n")
stopifnot("gene" %in% colnames(adata$obs))
```

```{r seurat}
counts <- t(adata$X)
stopifnot(inherits(counts, "sparseMatrix"))
rownames(counts) <- rownames(adata$var)
colnames(counts) <- rownames(adata$obs)
meta <- as.data.frame(adata$obs)
rownames(meta) <- colnames(counts)
obj <- CreateSeuratObject(counts=counts, meta.data=meta, project="Replogle_K562_CRISPRi")
cat("Sparse matrix:", class(counts)[1], "nonzero entries:", length(counts@x), "\n")
summary(obj$nCount_RNA)
summary(obj$nFeature_RNA)
```

### Interpretation

The source contains 310,385 cells and 8,563 genes. Count and detected-feature summaries are derived from the sparse expression matrix, which retains zero values without a dense allocation. These measures provide the basis for the recorded QC limits.

# QC and perturbation coverage

```{r qc}
qc <- read.csv("results/01_qc_report.csv")
qc
cat("Mitochondrial genes:", qc$mt_gene_count, "\n")
if (qc$mt_gene_count > 0) print(summary(obj$percent.mt))
VlnPlot(obj, features=c("nCount_RNA", "nFeature_RNA"), pt.size=0)
```

### Interpretation

QC retained 305,906 of 310,385 cells (98.6%), indicating modest rather than aggressive removal. Count and feature limits use the full-dataset 0.5% and 99.5% quantiles; 13 observed mitochondrial genes support the 20% mitochondrial ceiling. The violin plots describe the retained sample's QC distributions and do not independently establish biological quality.

```{r perturbation-coverage}
full_counts <- read.csv("results/01_perturbation_cell_counts.csv")
sample_counts <- read.csv("results/01_analysis_perturbation_counts.csv")
cat("Perturbations after QC:", nrow(full_counts), "\n")
cat("Perturbations in analysis:", nrow(sample_counts), "\n")
summary(sample_counts$n_cells)
ggplot(head(sample_counts, 25), aes(x=reorder(gene, n_cells), y=n_cells)) +
  geom_col() + coord_flip() + labs(x="Perturbation", y="Analysis cells") + theme_minimal()
```

### Interpretation

The seeded 12,000-cell subset retains all 2,058 post-QC perturbation labels, making it useful for broad coverage and global structure. Its median is five cells per label; the frequency plot highlights uneven representation, including 76 non-targeting cells. This subset is too sparse for reliable detailed differential expression across all targets.

```{r save}
saveRDS(obj, "data/processed/01_k562_qc_seurat.rds")
```

## Key results

```{r key-results}
cat("Full cells:", qc$before, "after QC:", qc$after, "analysis cells:", qc$analysis, "\n")
cat("Genes:", nrow(obj), "perturbations:", nrow(sample_counts), "\n")
```

- **Source data:** 310,385 cells × 8,563 genes provide the full public input.
- **QC-filtered data:** 305,906 cells (98.6%) remain after the recorded count, feature, and mitochondrial limits.
- **Broad coverage subset:** 12,000 seeded cells retain all 2,058 labels for global analysis, with limited per-target power.
